messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (us-west-2) for model redwood-7B-quant. Current 5xx rate 12% over baseline. Paging @maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): on it. seeing spike across multiple hosts in the model-runner pool. paging simon and ops. status?

simon: I’m pulling the model-runner logs now. grabbing pid and last crash traces. can someone post the ingress error histogram?

ops-bot: Ingress metrics: 5xxs started spiking at 2026-03-15T02:14:06Z, median latency up from 120ms -> 1.2s. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.

maya (oncall): simon any obvious OOMs or segfaults?

simon: yes, multiple runners showing segfaults and coredumps. here's a tail of the last crash from runner-42:

```
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] model-runner[pid=32145]: RuntimeError: kv_cache_resize(): attempted to allocate 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] model-runner[pid=32145]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f1c0d6f
[2026-03-15T02:15:22Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 32145 (model-runner) total-vm: 245M
```

maya (oncall): looks like memory blowup during long-context inference. is this a model variant rollout?

product-sre: Confirmed — rolling out redwood-7B-quant canary started 02:10Z with traffic ramp to 10%. Canary config increased max_sequence to 4096.

maya (oncall): that matches — kv cache growth + quant path might be hitting a bug. immediate mitigation: revert canary to stable variant and route traffic back. simon, can you push rollback?

simon: on it. running rollback via control-plane now:

```
# rollback canary
redwoodctl rollout rollback --target redwood-7B-quant --from canary
```

simon: rollback submitted. control-plane shows rollback accepted and routing updates queued. estimated traffic shift 30s.

maya (oncall): also we should scale runner ASG by +20% to absorb in-flight load while we watch. aaron, can you scale?

aaron: scaling runners now (group model-runner-usw2) -> desired +20%. Kubernetes: increasing replica count from 50 -> 60.

ops-bot: Pod restarts: 34, 37, 42, 45 had OOMKilled in last 5m. New pods are coming up.

lina: do we have an immediate customer-impact list? cs-rep, any reports?

cs-rep: CS queue: 7 tickets flagged urgent, 3 customers on dedicated capacity reported 5xxs and timeouts ~30s. Not widespread yet but a handful of high-traffic tenants. I’ll draft a short status note once we have confirmed rollback.

maya (oncall): good. simon — after rollback, please restart model-runner service on nodes that had coredumps to clear any bad state. use graceful drain where possible. commands:

```
kubectl rollout restart ds/model-runner -n inference
# or for affected nodes:
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
systemctl restart model-runner
kubectl uncordon <node>
```

simon: doing rolling restart now. restarting batch of 5 nodes at a time to avoid capacity cliffs.

maya (oncall): also temp policy: disable continuous batching for redwood-7B-quant paths to reduce memory amplification until we root cause. ops: can be toggled in runtime config.

ops-bot: Applied runtime config: continuous_batching=false for redwood-7B-quant canary traffic. Changes will hit runners in ~10s.

simon: rollback completed, routing back to stable model redwood-7B (non-quant). verifying metrics.

ops-bot: Routing switch complete at 2026-03-15T02:17:01Z. 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 3% within 60s. Latency trending back to baseline.

maya (oncall): nice. still seeing a few stragglers on older runners, keep restart in progress. simon, collect coredumps and upload to S3. attach logs with symbolized backtrace.

simon: collected cores and uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/INF-2026-042/cores/. sample backtrace points to memcpy in quant kernel, possible double-free in kv cache resize path.

maya (oncall): assigning incident id INF-2026-042. severity: sev2 (customer impact limited but real). i'll start the incident doc. Lina, Maya handing off oncall to you in 25m — i'll stay on the bridge for another 20 min then handover notes.

lina: standing by to take over. please add to incident doc any outstanding TODOs.

maya (oncall): TODOs:
- simon: analyze backtrace, reproduce locally with long-context run (sequence=4096).
- infra: complete rolling restarts and confirm node health metrics.
- product-sre: block canary variant and add safety limits (max_sequence default 2048).
- cs-rep: customer advisory draft for affected tenants.

simon: started reproducer in internal CI with instrumented allocator. early repro shows kv_cache_resize under quant path trips allocator threshold. working on minimal reproducer now. ETA 2-3h.

product-sre: we will add guardrail to control-plane to prevent canary configs > 2048 for this family until patch. noted.

cs-rep: drafting customer note now; will flag dedicated customers first. cc: account leads.

maya (oncall): good. Lina — once oncall, please continue monitoring for 1h and confirm 5xxs remain <1%. handoff: state in doc and attach link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2026-042

lina: ack. taking over monitoring and incident comms. simon — please ping when you have a reproducible test and I'll queue eng resources.

simon: will ping here. provisional owner for postmortem: @simon.

maya (oncall): leaving the channel — keeping bridge open for 15m in case anyone needs me. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Monitoring alert cleared for 5xx spike at 2026-03-15T02:25:10Z. Follow-up: schedule a deeper postmortem within 48h.

lina: noted. quick postmortem owners and timeline in doc. I'll post a short customer-facing status update in 15m.

cs-rep: posted customer advisory draft to shared doc, tagging account teams. link copied to incident doc.

maya (oncall): final note: root cause hypothesis - quant kernel + kv cache resize bug leading to memory corruption/segfault under long-context workload. mitigation path: rollback, restart, disable batching, and guardrail configs. further mitigation: patch quant allocator and add unit tests.

simon: agreed. starting deeper debug now. will file PR for a fix candidate and include perf/regression tests for large sequences.

lina: closing handoff. monitoring and comms on me. INF-2026-042 created.

product-sre: tagging this for release freeze of any quant rollouts until fix merged and canary safety gates improved.

cs-rep: updating affected customers that rollback completed and we're monitoring.

maya (oncall): thanks team — good triage and mitigation.

(End of thread)
